subject: FinCo Redwood evals - next steps
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: FinCo Data Science <datascience@finco.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: FinCo Redwood evals - next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side: FinCo wants to validate Redwood for our customer-facing document summarization and KYC question-answering flows. Key goals are:
- Quality parity with our current on-prem model (we'll provide a holdout dataset)
- Latency under 400ms for short Q&A (95th percentile)
- Cost targets per 1k queries (we'll share traffic profile)

Can you share recommended model families to evaluate, the dataset format you need, and scoring criteria you typically run? We also need guidance on how to securely upload our eval data (S3 vs. pre-signed uploads).

We'd like Redwood to run the evals if possible so we can compare real inference metrics (latency/cost) against your hosted profiles. Proposed timeline: initial evals in ~2 weeks. Can you confirm availability and next steps?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Lead Product Manager, FinCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@finco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinCo Redwood evals - next steps

Hi Alyssa —

Great to meet you earlier — really appreciate the clear goals. High-level answers and proposed next steps below.

Recommended models to evaluate (initial pass):
- redwood-chat-70b: best-in-class for summarization quality; higher cost.
- redwood-open-15b: strong quality/cost balance for summarization and Q&A.
- redwood-7b-quant: lower-cost baseline to test quantized inference tradeoffs.

We typically run the following on customer-specific evals on Redwood:
1) Functional accuracy: exact-match / ROUGE / BLEU where applicable (we'll tailor to your scoring matrix).
2) Semantic similarity: embedding-based cosine + manual spot checks for hallucination-prone cases.
3) Latency & throughput: measured on your traffic profile with continuous batching to estimate 95/99p latency.
4) Cost simulation: per-token and per-request cost using our quantized model profiles.

Attached: finco_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (example prompt set) and eval_scoring_matrix.xlsx (suggested scoring thresholds). The prompt set is JSONL with one record per line; each record should include: input (string), expected_output (string), and metadata (freeform). Example line in the attached: {"input": "Summarize the following customer email...", "expected_output": "Key points: ...", "metadata": {"case_id": "1234"}}

Data upload options: we support three patterns — 1) Secure S3 bucket (recommended), 2) Pre-signed upload link (time-limited), 3) Secure console upload via our private project page. If you can provide a cross-account S3 bucket or we can create a presigned URL, we will ingest the dataset into an isolated eval project. Please note retention defaults to 30 days unless you request otherwise.

Next steps / timeline:
- You: confirm preferred upload method and provide an example of 200–500 labeled records for pilot (aiming for a diverse sample).
- We (Redwood): create a dedicated eval project and spin up the evaluation runner using the three model families above; run functional + latency tests and share a results dashboard (ETA: 7 business days after data ingest).
- Joint: 30-min results review and action plan for production rollout.

If that works I'll have Neha and Dev own the onboarding and infra pieces. We can also schedule a short kickoff next week.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0134

Hi Alyssa —

I'll own the onboarding. Quick operational notes and the S3 steps:

1) S3 options:
   - Cross-account bucket: we can request read-only access; please add aws-account-id 123456789012 as a read principal and then email the bucket name.
   - Pre-signed upload: if you prefer not to change ACLs, we can generate a set of presigned POST URLs for the sample dataset.

2) Dataset format checklist (please ensure):
   - JSONL, UTF-8 encoded, one record per line.
   - Required fields: input, expected_output, case_id.
   - Max file size per object: 200MB. Tar.gz multiple files if larger.

3) Security & PII: redwood-chat-70b runs in an isolated project with KMS encryption at rest. We recommend masking direct identifiers; if you need we can enable additional tokenization filters during eval ingestion.

4) Scoring thresholds (from the attached matrix):
   - Summarization: ROUGE-L >= 0.45 OR human quality >= 4/5 for production consideration.
   - Q&A exact match >= 78% for high-confidence intents.

5) Next steps / scheduling:
   - Share S3 bucket name or request presigned links by 2026-12-11 EOD.
   - We will ingest and run pilot eval (300 records) and deliver a dashboard within 7 business days.
   - Proposed kickoff: 2026-12-14 10:00 AM PT (30 min). I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

If you want, Dev can provide temporary runner capacity estimates so you can see cost projections before we run the full sweep.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
